questions: Are rows and columns indexed from 1 (as implied by i=1..N) or from 0? The output lines are labeled i-th row, but the indexing for cell positions in the algorithm uses 1-based.
The clarification says 'Standard convention applies here' but doesn't specify indexing convention. Should we assume 1-based indexing for both input description and output row numbering?
Is the grid N×N defined with rows and columns both numbered 1..N, and cell (i,j) means row i, column j?
What should happen if N is even and i = j for an even i? The region is a single cell at (i,i) with i even, so it should be white. Is that correct?

The operation says 'fill the rectangular region whose top-left cell is (i,i) and bottom-right cell is (j,j)'. Does 'fill' mean color all cells within that inclusive rectangle, i.e., rows i..j and columns i..j?
For i ≤ j, we fill the square from (i,i) to (j,j). If i > j, we do nothing. But what about when i = j? That's a 1×1 square. Is it handled correctly?

The output format says 'Print N lines. The i-th line should contain a length-N string S_i representing the colors of the i-th row of the grid'. Is the first line printed corresponding to row 1 or row 0?
Are there any constraints on N beyond 1 ≤ N ≤ 50? For example, is N guaranteed to be odd? The pattern example shows N=11 (odd).
